Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexlify Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Today's call is being recorded. At the request of Nexlify, this conference is being recorded for replay purposes. If you have any objections, please disconnect at this time. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Nexlify's Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; Casey Wong, Chief Product Officer; and Riley Chen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. These statements are based on our current expectations, but actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Nexlify's outstanding performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by robust demand for our Nexlify IQ AI suite and continued execution of our strategic initiatives across enterprise workflow automation.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: our product roadmap, NRR performance, gross margin expansion, LTV/CAC ratio improvements, full-year revenue guidance, average contract value trends, and capital allocation strategy.

These efforts propelled us forward, with product-led growth fueling a 28% year-over-year increase in dollar-based net retention to 118%, strong operational leverage, and positioning us for sustained leadership in the $120 billion workflow automation market. Jordan will dive deeper into these metrics and our financial results shortly.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a truly strong quarter across the board. Revenue for the quarter came in at $125 million, representing a 30% increase year-over-year. Our GAAP gross margin expanded to 78.5%, and non-GAAP gross margin reached 81.2%. Operating income stood at $30 million, reflecting healthy profitability.

Let me unpack these results and the key areas Alex mentioned, starting with gross margin performance, which continues to be a standout for our scalable, multi-tenant cloud-native architecture serving over 5,000 customers—from mid-market to Fortune 500—processing billions of workflows annually.

For Q3 FY24, GAAP gross margin was 78.5%, up 230 basis points year-over-year from 76.2% and 60 basis points sequentially from Q2. Non-GAAP came in at 81.2%, with 320 basis points YoY improvement. This leverage stems from efficiencies in hosting and infrastructure, which are about 65% of cost of revenue. Hosting costs dropped from 18.4% to 15.2% of revenue YoY, thanks to our hybrid AWS-Google Cloud migration using committed discounts and reserved instances for a 22% cut in per-TB compute. We also rolled out Kubernetes auto-scaling and AI-driven predictive planning, hitting 92% utilization during peaks, while generative AI inference costs fell 35% via model distillation and edge caching, all while upholding 99.99% SLAs.

Sequentially, a slight uptick from GPU ramps for new AI features was offset by volume leverage from 28% ARR growth to roughly $1.4 billion annualized. Product mix helped too—our 118% DBNR drove expansion in high-margin enterprise segments like financial services and healthcare, now 42% of ARR with margins over 85%. We de-emphasized lower-margin SMB self-serve, aligning with peers like Atlassian.

Regionally, North America at 62% of revenue hit 82.1% margins; EMEA grew to 22% share with 42% YoY growth and 77.8% margins via GDPR features and new Frankfurt-Dublin nodes; APAC at 16% with 55% growth is at 73.4% but converging with localized language models. Our 'Margin First' approach, with RPO at $2.8 billion up 35% YoY, dynamic pricing yielding 12-15% uplift on renewals, and pro services at 8%, keeps gross dollar churn at 4.2%. We expect Q4 GAAP at 79-80%, expanding further into FY25.

Turning to NRR performance, we delivered 117% for Q3 FY24, up sequentially from 115% in Q2 and 5 points YoY from 112%. From a $285 million cohort MRR base, we retained and expanded to $334 million. Expansion added 28 points, up from 25, via 12% ACV growth per expander and cross-sells—ForgeAI Analytics, akin to Salesforce Einstein, drove 42% of expansions, with premium ForgeConnect adding 18% seats in mid-market.

Churn held at 4% annualized, down 100 bps YoY, with NPS up 20% to 68 from health scoring flagging risks 45 days early. Logo churn 2.5% in small SMBs we sunsetted; enterprise near-zero at 0.8% with 65% multi-year contracts. Contraction subtracted 7 points, improved from 9, via pay-for-performance pilots retaining 30% of downgrades. North America 72% ARR at 120%; EMEA 119% up 400 bps with London DC; APAC 108% but improving via Alibaba partnerships. Platformization lifted modules per customer to 4.1; usage pricing now 28% of revenue accelerates expansions 15%. Q4 guide 116-119%, top-quartile positioning.

On average contract value, ACV hit $48,200 in Q3, up 25% YoY from $38,600 and 7% QoQ from $45,100—10th straight quarter of growth. Enterprise over $100K averaged $162,000, +32% YoY, with six $500K+ deals including a $1.2M Fortune 100 fin serv suite bundling CRM, analytics, and Nexlify AI CoPilot. Enterprise now 42% of bookings. Mid-market $52,400 +15% via Revenue Intelligence-Snowflake integrations; SMB $14,800 +12% with no-code bundles. North America $55,400 +28%; EMEA $42,100 +35%; APAC $38,200 +18%. Nexlify AI CoPilot drove 22% expansion revenue, $35K uplift average, 3x faster ROI; multi-product at 65% of enterprise. Dynamic AI pricing 15-20% premiums, discounting <8%. Q4 ACV 20-25% YoY growth expected.

Our LTV/CAC ratio strengthened to 4.2x, up from 3.8x QoQ and 3.2x YoY—elite tier like Snowflake, above 3x median. LTV at $48,000 for recent cohorts via 128% NRR and 92% gross retention; ForgeGuard ML cuts churn 22% QoQ. CAC steady at $11,400 despite 12% CPL rises, via PLG freemium viral 1.4x, inbound 45% pipeline, Salesforce co-sell 25% logos, 9-month payback. North America 4.5x; EMEA 4.0x +45% DACH; APAC 3.5x improving. Guide 4.5x+ YE via AI ARPU +20%, CAC compression, hyperscaler logos. Cohorts tracking 4.8x.

Shifting to our product roadmap, we're executing to drive ARR growth and leadership. Nexlify IQ beta exceeded, 65% adoption post-GA driving 22% active workflows. IQ 2.0 Q3 rollout brings agentic AI for autonomous triage—e.g., Salesforce/HubSpot CRM ingest, 92% deal velocity prediction on 10TB data, auto-outreach. Fintech pilots cut sales cycles 35%, $450K ARR uplift; $15/seat + usage, $18M Q2 ARR (12% total). Q4 IQ 3.0 multimodal for docs, like Claude 3, legal/healthcare. Composable arch 3x faster builds; 150+ Q2 connectors (Snowflake, Okta), 1,200 partners, API +150%. Enterprise Scale-Out GA for 1M TPS Kubernetes, 40% infra savings AWS EKS, 99.999% uptime. NA 62% ARR; EMEA 22% +45% GDPR zones Frankfurt/Paris; APAC +60% QoQ India Jio/rupee pricing $15B opp. Q3 Industry Clouds: Retail RFID, Fin SOX, Mfg MES; hybrid outcome pricing, 28% faster TTV, sub-5% churn verticals. $250M FY24 capex (25% opex) R&D, 40% AI/security; NPS 68 from 52.

For capital allocation, with $850 million cash, $300M FCF Q3 +28% YoY, we're positioned amid 7-9x SaaS multiples. Prioritize Rule of 40 at 48% (22% growth, 26% FCF margin), NRR >115%, 82% gross. Pillars: R&D 24% revenue/$180M Q3 for multimodal LLMs (Anthropic/OpenAI), Creator AI 35% faster; $40M APAC localization PIPL. M&A: two $450M tuck-ins; Q2 $320M SecuraFlow zero-trust, $45M ARR 7x, $12M cross-sell. Eye 2-3 more $600-800M HR/predictive, EMEA fintech €50B TAM. Repos $150M Q3/$1.5B auth, 1.2M shares $185 avg. Debt $300M revolver 4.8%, 0.8x net debt/EBITDA. Capex 3% multi-cloud PoPs Singapore/São Paulo LatAm +45%. 60% growth levers, 25% returns, 15% flexibility; 35% FCF reinvest. $1.5B+ deployable YE.

Finally, full-year guidance: raising/narrowing to $480-495 million, 32-36% YoY midpoint $487.5M, +$30M prior. Subscription 34-37% growth; NRR 115-120%; net new ARR $140-155M; pricing +$8-10M. RPO current $650M +42%, future $1.2B +35%, 85% converts 12mo. Op margin 18-20% +300bps. Americas 75% 30-33%; EMEA 15% 45%; APAC 10% 55%. $120M R&D 25% revenue zero-ETL/agentic AI $100B TAM. Cash $750M no debt M&A tuck-ins. Risks sales cycles/forex.

We continue to invest heavily in R&D to drive innovation and expand offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $850 million, providing flexibility for strategic acquisitions and growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress advancing our AI capabilities, deeply integrating them into the Nexlify core platform. Adoption of Nexlify IQ features is soaring, boosting user engagement and customer outcomes like faster sales cycles and predictive insights. We've enhanced platform security with zero-trust integrations post-CrowdStrike and scalability for enterprise demands, supporting 1M+ TPS via Kubernetes and new edge nodes.

And now Casey Wong will update on the product roadmap.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Taylor. We've prioritized user experience, excited to launch Nexlify IQ 2.0 with agentic AI agents for autonomous workflows. This delivers 35% sales cycle reductions and 3x faster builds, aligning perfectly with our strategy—65% adoption already driving $18M ARR.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Casey. This quarter, our focus sharpened on brand awareness and lead gen via targeted digital campaigns and partnerships. We achieved a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% rise in qualified leads, proving our initiatives' impact amid competitive dynamics.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of Nexlify IQ on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. Nexlify IQ has been transformative, contributing $18M in new ARR this quarter—12% of total bookings—with 65% adoption among customers exceeding betas. Attach rates hit 65%, driving 22% more workflows per seat and 42% of expansions, far surpassing expectations like early pilots' 35% cycle reductions and $450K ARR uplifts. Competitively, our agentic AI outperforms legacy BPM like Pega/Appian, with proprietary models on 10TB data giving edge over Salesforce Einstein in workflow specificity; integrations ecosystem 1,200+ partners widens moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. International is accelerating—EMEA +45% to 22% ARR, APAC +60% QoQ to 16%. APAC focus: India ($15B SaaS TAM, Jio/rupee pricing), Japan (localized GTM Alibaba Cloud), ANZ compliance. Investments in Tokyo DC, Hindi/Japanese models target doubling $150M run-rate by FY25. ROI: 3-4x over 18-24 months via 55% growth, LTV/CAC to 4x+, NRR 108% improving.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn contained at 4% annualized, flat QoQ down 100bps YoY—logo 2.5% SMB-focused, enterprise 0.8%. NRR trended to 117% Q3, sequential up from 115%, broad-based NA 120%, EMEA 119%. Retention via 20% NPS lift to 68, CS health scoring 45-day flags, multi-year 65% ARR, ForgeGuard ML -22% voluntary churn. Pricing pilots pay-for-performance retained 30% contractions, dynamic 12-15% renewals no churn hit—gross retention 92-98%, expansions capture 85% overages.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Product roadmap: Provide updates on key product initiatives and feature launches.
NRR performance: Report NRR and explain drivers (expansion, contraction, churn).
Gross margin: Report gross margin and explain changes from prior periods.
LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Full-year revenue guidance: Provide revenue guidance for the full fiscal year.
Average contract value (ACV): Report and explain trends in average contract value.
Capital allocation: Discuss capital allocation strategy (investments, acquisitions, etc.).
